text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts observed from regional edge (eu-central1) since 02:07 UTC. Error rate spike: 5xx 18% -> 42% in 5m, p99 latency up 2.7x. Paging on-call: @Sam O'Neil :rotating_light:
Sam O'Neil: on it, picking up page. any customer-facing outages yet?
Jenny Alvarez: Support noticing timeouts for a subset of EU customers hitting /v1/generate — intermittent 504s. I have two active tickets (cust-A, cust-C) escalating.
Mike Chen: I'm pulling router + gateway metrics now. Looks like backend pool for eu-central1-gateway has high connection errors and TLS handshake failures to runtime instances. Could be a VPN flap or NAT exhaustion?
Alex G.: sharing logs from gateway-02: ```ERROR: upstream reset streaming: code=IO_ERROR, conn_id=3421, remote=10.12.5.6:8443``` Also seeing a burst of SYN_RECV on gateway hosts.
Sam O'Neil: good catch. Priority: reduce customer impact. Actions: 1) divert traffic from eu-central1 to eu-west1/us-east1 2) increase gateway pool in EU if possible 3) enable fallback routing to smaller model variant to reduce backend load. I'll request the routing change now.
Sam O'Neil: (runbook) routing change command: ```redwood route set-policy --region eu-central1 --policy fallback --fallback-region eu-west1 --weight 0.2``` Applying with gradual shift (20% -> 100% if stable).
deploy-bot: NOTICE: Route policy change initiated by Sam O'Neil. Change id: rcp-20260314-12.
Mike Chen: while traffic shifts, I'm spinning up additional gateway replicas in eu-central1 and checking kernel conntrack. Running: ```sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144``` and bumping worker threads for envoy.
Alex G.: also enabling prefix KV cache bypass for chat workloads in EU to avoid cache thrash: ```redwood runtime-config set --region eu-central1 --kv-cache disabled``` Expect regen hits but reduces heavy cache contention.
Ethan (support): I posted an update to affected customers explaining we're routing traffic and investigating. Sample message: "We're seeing increased timeouts in EU — we are routing to healthy regions and will update in 15m."
Priya (acct): flagging for accounts: I'm ready to reach out to strategic customers if this persists beyond 30m. Please ping me before customer outreach.
Mike Chen: I'm also seeing elevated egress from a specific host 10.12.5.6 — suspect network appliance flapping. Working with infra to cordon the host. Command: ```ssh ops@10.12.5.6 'sudo systemctl stop redwood-gateway'```
Sam O'Neil: cordon and drain complete, removed host 10.12.5.6 from rotation. Early metrics: 20% drop in 5xx in eu-central1 within 4m. Continue to monitor.
Alex G.: verification logs show connection success rates improving. Still seeing some TLS handshake timeouts from the NAT pool. Recommend increasing ephemeral port range on gateway nodes as a follow-up.
Jenny Alvarez: Support: new ticket notes — customers see short spikes, but most traffic recovered after routing change. Two customers still hitting errors (cust-C high QPS).
Sam O'Neil: mitigation summary so far: - traffic drifted to eu-west1 (20% -> 60%) - cordoned bad gateway host - increased conntrack and worker threads - enabled KV-cache bypass
Sam O'Neil: next steps: 1) if 5xx < 5% for 10m, continue rollback plan to return traffic incrementally. 2) If not, increase fallback -> send more to us-east1 and consider forced failover.
Mike Chen: adding temporary rate limiting for heavy customers in EU to protect the control plane: ```redwood quota set --customer cust-C --region eu-central1 --requests-per-minute 1200```
deploy-bot: NOTICE: Quota change applied by Mike Chen. change id q-20260314-07.
Ethan (support): cust-C on a Slack escalation channel; they confirmed errors continue for some endpoints. Sending logs to Mike.
Alex G.: collected tcpdump from gateway subnet and uploading to shared S3: s3://redwood-dumps/1768501234/gw-tcpdump.pcap.gz
Sam O'Neil: After 12m, eu-central1 5xx dropped to 6.8%, p99 latency trending down. I'm going to increase traffic back to 80% over 5 mins.
Sam O'Neil: routing update command: ```redwood route adjust --change-id rcp-20260314-12 --target-weight 0.8 --duration 300```
incident-bot: UPDATE: Change rcp-20260314-12 progressed to 80% traffic to eu-central1.
Jenny Alvarez: Support update posted to customers — most reported improvement. I'll keep monitoring the two open tickets.
Priya (acct): good. I'll stand by for any executive asks.
Mike Chen: follow-up remediation items: - investigate NAT/gateway appliance health and kernel limits - add automated drain for conntrack spikes - add alert for TLS handshake rate > 5%
Alex G.: small follow-up config to increase ephemeral ports on gateways: ```sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range='1024 65535'``` Planned as a change in next maintenance window unless we need immediate hotfix.
Sam O'Neil: handing off to Mike for long-term remediation. I'll mark incident as mitigated and start a 1:1 postmortem doc. On-call handoff: @Mike Chen now primary.
Mike Chen: taking over. I'll collect the detailed timeline and coordinate infra for the host replacement. ETA: 2 hours for full host replacement and NAT pool validation.
Ethan (support): I'll update customers that we're in remediation and will provide a detailed incident timeline once available.
incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity downgraded to S2.
Sam O'Neil: thanks team. Postmortem owners: Mike Chen (tech), Jenny Alvarez (customer comms), Priya (acct impact). We'll sync at 17:00 UTC for RCA.
Priya (acct): noted. I'll prepare the customer impact report with affected org list and monthly usage impact.
Mike Chen: collecting artifacts now: route change IDs, gateway logs, conntrack metrics, tcpdumps. Will attach to postmortem doc.
Jenny Alvarez: closing loop on support tickets: cust-A resolved, cust-C pending but stable.
Sam O'Neil: locking thread for incident chat — move follow-ups to #incidents-postmortem and link doc when ready. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
